jupas.shortDescription: an class="before_label">Short Description The Department of Chinese Language and Literature, which has the longest history at CUHK, is renowned for its excellence in preserving tradition and striving for innovation. The Department offers rigorous training in Chinese language and literature. The curriculum affords a close examination of the characteristic features of the Chinese language, an in-depth introduction to theories of language and linguistics, and critical study of classical and modern Chinese literature. Students are expected to acquire solid understanding of the field in general while specialising in their own areas of interest, such as Chinese phonology and grammar, Qin-Han textual studies, Tang-Song poetry, modern Chinese fiction, and creative writing— all under the guidance of our erudite faculty members. The Department has long been emphasising diversified learning. We are collaborating with the Department of Chinese Language and Literature at Peking University to offer a dual undergraduate degree programme starting from 2019/20, which could combine the advantages of the both institutions to strengthen the learning experience of our students. In the academic year 2022/23, a double major programme in partnership with the Department of Translation (CHLL&TRANS) was introduced. This programme caters to students with a keen interest in both the theory and practice of C to E (Chinese to English) and E to C (English to Chinese) translation.

cuhkAdmission.introduction: Explore Your Journey with Our Chinese Language and Literature Programme The Department of Chinese Language and Literature offers rigorous training in Chinese language and literature. Our curriculum offers a detailed exploration of the unique characteristics of the Chinese language, an in-depth introduction to theories of language and linguistics, and critical study of ancient documents, and both classical and modern literature. Our students are expected to develop a strong foundational understanding of the field in general while specialising in their own areas of interest, providing a broad perspective, and they are free to choose and study topics of interest in various areas in Chinese language and literature. The programme has the following features: (1) core course requirements that establish a solid foundation for further study in Chinese language and literature; (2) more than 50 specialty courses, allowing students to tailor their academic journey and align it with their interests; (3) small-group teaching in creative-writing courses, fostering close teacher-student relationships; (4) a core course of independent research for final-year students, in which they learn research methodologies and critical approaches by planning and conducting research on a topic in preparation for a thesis written under the close supervision of a faculty member; and (5) writing courses that enhance the students’ creative-writing skills, resulting in our students consistently achieving recognition and awards in major literary competitions. Our graduates display an excellent command of both written and spoken Chinese, are well-versed in the great traditions of Chinese literature, and are thoroughly prepared to take on new challenges as they embark on their professional or academic careers.
cuhkAdmission.careerProspects: Our Chinese Language and Literature programme goes beyond traditional classroom learning, providing students with immersive experiences in the realm of Chinese language and literature. These experiences encompass global exchanges, internships, and study-abroad opportunities, allowing students to apply theoretical knowledge to real-world situations. Literary and philological concepts are brought to life through enriching internships, nurturing skills in critical analysis, effective communication and interpersonal relationships. As graduates, students emerge with a solid academic foundation and versatile skills that enable them to excel in a wide range of professional sectors, including business, government, media and community service. Their achievements stand as a testament to the programme’s capability to prepare individuals for excellence and accomplishment. Education Sector: approximately 82.1% enter education. Business Sector: about 10.3% enter business, excelling in management and publishing. Postgraduate Studies: around 44.4% pursue specialized fields through advanced studies. [Figures as of December 2023] For those with aspirations to advance their careers within the Chinese Language and Literature programme, postgraduate studies provide additional avenues for growth. Our dedicated faculty, deeply invested in our students’ success, offer career consultation that provides individuals with vital skills and profound insights. Beyond traditional education, our programme in Chinese Language and Literature nurtures versatile professionals, prepared to excel in a dynamic world brimming with boundless opportunities. If you are interested in this programme, please review the application requirements and deadlines specific to the respective admission scheme to increase your chances of getting accepted. APPLY NOW
cuhkAdmission.craftYourPath: Craft your academic voyage in Chinese literature by shaping a curriculum that resonates with your literary passion. Evoke Your Inquisitiveness – Embrace a rich array of courses, and embark on a voyage of self-discovery through the world of Chinese literature. Pursue Literary Excellence – Immerse yourself deeply in your chosen realm of Chinese literary artistry, refining your expertise along the way. Diversified Programmes The Department is collaborating with the Department of Chinese Language and Literature at Peking University to offer a dual undergraduate degree programme starting in the 2019/20 academic year, which combines the advantages of both institutions to enhance the learning experience of our students. In the 2022/23 academic year, we expanded our offerings with a double major programme, in collaboration with CUHK’s Department of Translation. This programme caters for students with a keen interest in both the theory and practice of C to E (Chinese to English) and E to C (English to Chinese) translation. It’s designed to provide a comprehensive experience for students seeking expertise in translation within the context of Chinese literature and language studies.
